[[File:Lyubomir-Ivanov.jpg|thumb|right|Self-portrait, 2004]]
'''Lyubomir Ivanov''' ({{langx|bg|Любомир Иванов}}, born 7 October 1952 in [[Sofia]]) is a Bulgarian scientist, non-governmental activist, and [[Antarctica|Antarctic]] explorer.  He is a graduate of the [[St. Kliment Ohridski]] [[Sofia University|University of Sofia]] with M.S. degree in [[mathematics]] in 1977. He earned his PhD from [[Sofia University]] in 1980, under the direction of [[Dimiter Skordev]] with a dissertation titled ''Iterative Operative Spaces'', and was the 1987 winner of ''Acad. Nikola Obreshkov Prize'', the highest Bulgarian award in mathematics.<ref>[[:File:Nikola-Obreshkov-Prize.png|The ''Academician Nikola Obreshkov Prize'' for 1987]]</ref>

==Academic and NGO work==
Appointed head of the [[Department of Mathematical Logic (Bulgarian Academy of Sciences)|Department of Mathematical Logic]] at the [[Institute of Mathematics and Informatics (Bulgarian Academy of Sciences)|Institute of Mathematics and Informatics]], [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] in 1990, Ivanov has since helped found the [[Atlantic Club of Bulgaria]], in which he held the position of chairman from 2001 to 2009. In 1994, he founded the [[Manfred Wörner Foundation]], an organisation dedicated to trans-atlantic co-operation. He was a member of the Streit Council Advisory Board, Washington, DC since 2006<ref>{{cite web
 |title=The Streit Council: Our Mission 
 |publisher=Association to Unite the Democracies 
 |date=28 July 2008 
 |url=http://www.streitcouncil.org/content/about_us/board.html 
 |format=ISO-8859-1 
 |accessdate=18 August 2008 
 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080625194118/http://www.streitcouncil.org/content/about_us/board.html 
 |archivedate=25 June 2008 
 |url-status=dead 
}}
</ref> and, founding Chairman, [[Antarctic Place-names Commission]] since 1994.<ref>J. Stewart. [https://epdf.tips/antarctica-an-encyclopedia-2-volume-set-second-edition.html ''Antarctica: An Encyclopedia''.] Jefferson, N.C. and London: McFarland, 2011. 1771 pp.</ref><ref>{{Cite web
 |last        = Kalchev
 |first       = Victor
 |title       = Who is who in Bulgarian Politic: Lyubomir . Ivanov, Atlantic Club of Bulgaria – President
 |url         = http://www.online.bg/asp/politicianENG.asp?n1=Lyubomir&n2=.&n3=Ivanov
 |accessdate  = 7 August 2017
 |url-status     = bot: unknown
 |archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20070927173259/http://www.online.bg/asp/politicianENG.asp?n1=Lyubomir&n2=.&n3=Ivanov
 |archivedate = 27 September 2007}}
</ref> He authored the modern Bulgarian system for [[Romanization of Bulgarian|Romanization of Cyrillic alphabet]],<ref>Ivanov, L., D. Skordev and D. Dobrev. [https://web.archive.org/web/20160210095151/http://www.fmi.uni-sofia.bg/fmi/logic/skordev/B1-Ivanov-Skordev-Dobrev.pdf The New National Standard for the Romanization of Bulgarian.] ''Mathematica Balkanica''. New Series Vol. 24, 2010, Fasc. 1–2. pp.&nbsp;121–130. ISSN 0205-3217</ref> adopted also for official use both by UN,<ref>[http://www.eki.ee/wgrs/rom1_bg.htm Report on the Current Status of United Nations Romanization Systems for Geographical Names.] Compiled by the UNGEGN Working Group on Romanization Systems, February 2013.</ref> and also by the US and UK.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160210101058/http://geonames.nga.mil/gns/html/Romanization/Romanization_Bulgarian.pdf Romanization system for Bulgarian: BGN/PCGN 2013 System.] National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, September 2014.</ref>

In the course of his work for, among others, the Atlantic Club of Bulgaria, Ivanov has given interviews to various news outlets, at times espousing views that NATO must expand eastwards due to a deficit in its military capacity.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulgaria and the world|publisher=Radio Bulgaria|date=19 March 2008|url=http://www.bnr.bg/RadioBulgaria/Emission_English/Theme_Bulgaria_And_The_World/Material/AlBal.htm|accessdate=18 August 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080617164400/http://www.bnr.bg/RadioBulgaria/Emission_English/Theme_Bulgaria_And_The_World/Material/AlBal.htm|archive-date=17 June 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Political career==
Ivanov was a member of the [[Union of Democratic Forces (Bulgaria)|UDF]] Coordinating Council<ref>[https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/UDF_Coordinating_Council_1990 List of members of the Coordinating Council of the Union of Democratic Forces.] ''Demokratsiya Newspaper'', 27 April 1990.</ref> and took part in the 1990 [[Bulgarian Round Table Talks]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20191230092725/http://www.omda.bg/public/bulg/k_masa/2301a/1.html National Round Table: First Plenary Session.] National Palace of Culture Hall # 6, 23 January 1990 (Full transcript)</ref> He served as a Member of Parliament in Bulgaria (1990–1991), acting as Chairman of the Green Party parliamentary group, and co-authored the current [[Constitution of Bulgaria]]. He has also served as parliamentary secretary for the Bulgarian ministry of foreign affairs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Academic Refugee Studies Initiative in Bulgaria |publisher=United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR) |date=24 October 2002 |url=http://www.unhcr.bg/events_records/2002/un_day_24oct02/un_day_24oct02_en.pdf |accessdate=14 May 2005|url-status=unfit |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20050514165705/http://www.unhcr.bg/events_records/2002/un_day_24oct02/un_day_24oct02_en.pdf |archivedate=14 May 2005 }}</ref>

==Antarctic expeditions==
Ivanov has taken part in several Antarctic expeditions. In 2004, Ivanov went with [[Doychin Vasilev]] on the [[Tangra 2004/05]] topographic expedition, noted by [[Discovery Channel (UK and Ireland)|Discovery Channel]], the [[Natural History Museum, London|Natural History Museum]], the [[Royal Collection]] and the [[British Antarctic Survey]] as a timeline event in Antarctic exploration.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pole Expedition List |publisher=ThePoles.com |url=http://www.thepoles.com/page/2004Antarctica.htm |accessdate=8 March 2005 |url-status=unfit |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20050308131630/http://www.thepoles.com/page/2004Antarctica.htm |archivedate=8 March 2005 }}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150702022912/http://www.discoveryuk.com/web/discovering-antarctica ''Discovering Antarctica Overview''.] Discovery Channel UK website, 2012</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150629181745/http://www.discoveryuk.com/web/discovering-antarctica/timeline/ 14 November 2004: Tangra. ''Discovering Antarctica Timeline''.] Discovery Channel UK website, 2012</ref> Awarded the jubilee medal [[:File:Medal-30th-Bulgarian-Antarctic-Expedition-Certificate.png|''30th Bulgarian Antarctic Expedition'']] by the [[Bulgarian Antarctic Institute]]  for his active participation in the expeditions and in the building of [[St. Kliment Ohridski base|St. Kliment Ohridski polar base]]. He took part, inter alia, in the first Bulgarian landing on [[Smith Island (South Shetland Islands)|Smith Island]] in 2025.<ref>Y. Minkova. [https://web.archive.org/web/20260404133548/https://www.naval-acad.bg/2025/7593?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTEAc3J0YwZhcHBfaWQMMjU2MjgxMDQwNTU4AAEePesqQ14gWctdO_VjHZ-YZYiMtbk26t7ZhsNJuj-4HRisaF90UaCTWXkZfe4_aem_VDchvPynrjAS3mQsES88IA Research and Survey Vessel ''Sts. Cyril and Methodius'' at Smith Island]. ''Nikola Vaptsarov'' Naval Academy, Varna, 12 January 2025. (in Bulgarian)</ref>
<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20260403133330/https://bnrnews.bg/en/post/123462/bulgarians-explore-smith-island-in-antarctica Bulgarians explore Smith Island in Antarctica]. Radio Bulgaria in English, 13 January 2025.</ref><ref>D. Maneva. [https://web.archive.org/web/20260405060135/https://360mag.bg/posts/152262 Bulgarians landed on the most inaccessible island in the area of Western Antarctica]. ''360° Magazine'', 14 January 2025. (in Bulgarian)</ref>
